name: Lake of the Woods Bouldering
parking_note: Drive east out of Hope on Highway 1 for a couple of minutes; a small lot sits at the lake on the left side of the road.

name: Upper Cat Wall
parking_note: Leave the car at the lakeside pullout with a red gate, about 1 km past the dam when driving in from Castlegar or Nelson on the road toward Robson.

name: Upper Slide
parking_note: From Mission, drive Highway 7 east to Morris Valley Road, then turn onto the forest service road at the first four-way stop. Follow it along the lake to the far end and park at the large pullout near the boulders.

name: Mt. Woodside
parking_note: Turn onto Woodside Mountain Road opposite the Woodside Mountain Inn off Highway 7 and drive up the gravel road for about 10 to 15 minutes until the bluff shows on your right. A wide gravel pullout there holds many vehicles; a high-clearance or 4x4 vehicle is recommended.

name: Tulip Falls
parking_note: Drive Broadwater Road to Syringa Provincial Park, stay right on the Deer Park forest road and follow it for about 4 km. Park in the pullout on the right.

name: Begay Boulder
parking_note: Drive 2.6 miles along NP230 and pull off at the two large boulders on the left; the bigger one has the name Begay carved into it.

name: 2nd Gate Wall
parking_note: Drive east on 1800/1900 North from Logan to the canyon mouth, then up the canyon road a little over a mile; park at campsite 7, directly in front of Devil's Cave where most routes are. Inverted Stairway is across the road a short way up.

name: Sand Traverse Boulder (AKA The Mushroom Boulder), The
Pinnacle on North Ridge of Peak 11,158, West of Ruth Lake
Cabbage Patch
parking_note: Pull off along the canyon road about a quarter mile uphill from the Secret Garden boulders, on the north side. The boulders stand just inside the trees from the roadside.

name: Kelly's Rock
parking_note: From the Woodbury Road turnoff, drive the graded dirt road a little under four miles and pull in on the right just beyond the fourth cattle guard. The same lot serves Black and Tan.

name: Campsite 7
parking_note: Drive east on 1800/1900 North from Logan to the canyon mouth, then up the canyon road a little over a mile; park at campsite 7, directly in front of Devil's Cave where most routes are. Inverted Stairway is across the road a short way up.

name: Compound, The
parking_note: Without four-wheel drive, stop at the upper end of the smooth part of the canyon road near the Right Fork trailhead. High-clearance vehicles can sometimes go farther up the rough road.

name: Dust Bunny Boulder
parking_note: Drive east on 1800/1900 North from Logan to the canyon mouth, then up the canyon road a little over a mile; park at campsite 7, directly in front of Devil's Cave where most routes are. Inverted Stairway is across the road a short way up.

name: Entrance Wall, The
parking_note: Drive 0.8 mi up Maple Canyon Road from the canyon mouth, where the pavement turns to dirt, and park at one of several roadside pullouts. The land is private; a small donation for parking is requested.

name: How the Light Gets In Boulder
Lower Jungle
parking_note: A flat rocky pullout on the right side of the forest road, with room for roughly five cars; the road is dirt, and clearance helps.

name: Man Size
parking_note: Drive up the Right Fork road, about 0.9 miles from the canyon mouth. The largest roadside pullout on the fork serves the boulders, with a campground area and portable toilets at the same spot.

name: Mouth of Long Canyon Offwidth Boulders (MOLCOW area)
Shady Side
parking_note: Pull off at an unmarked wide spot beside Highway 18, a couple of miles north of the Sunset Boulevard junction. A short walk along the fence line leads to the top of the shady wall, and a quick scramble drops into the gully.

name: Sinbad Wall aka Nuclear Wall
parking_note: Gravel pullouts sit along the road on either side of the buttress, between Battle of the Bulge and Scorpion Corner.

name: Wall Street
parking_note: Park at the informal pull-offs along the Potash Road (UT 279), about 2 miles in from US-191; the routes are right beside the road. Park well out of the traffic lane, as potash trucks and 4x4s use it.

name: Anarchy Wall
parking_note: Use the pullout on the south side of the highway right after the third tunnel.

name: Mt. Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans), North Face
Water Groove Area (top of Kill Hill)
Arsenal, The
parking_note: Park right at the base of the routes in the cave itself, or use a pullout by the river a bit farther down the road.

name: Dungeon, The
parking_note: Most climbers start at the Lazy V lot inside Staunton State Park; if it is full, use the Meadow lot nearer the entrance and accept a longer hike in.

name: Bauhaus Wall
parking_note: Leave the car in a pullout on the right of the canyon road, roughly eight-tenths of a mile beyond the park entrance.

name: Bear Creek Cave, The
parking_note: Drive Bear Creek Rd (CO 74) about 1.1 miles west of the CO 8 junction and park on the left after the S bend, near the small bridge.

name: Olympic Wall
parking_note: Leave the car at the Grotto Walls pullout on the pass road, then walk the highway shoulder to a small cairn on the left that marks the climbers' path.

name: Lower Wall
parking_note: Use the large pull-out on the roadside about 300 feet east of the Glenwood Springs tunnel; the crag is visible from the pavement.

name: Boxcar Boulder
parking_note: Leave the car in the winter parking lot on the dirt road roughly 1.5 miles beyond the Wild Basin entrance gate. It is the only lot with room on both sides of the road. Do not continue past the creek bridge.

name: Buick Rocks and Hitler's Sex Life
parking_note: Drive County Road 80 about 0.6 mile past the Shelly Cottage turnoff, just beyond the Entryway Slabs, and use a pullout on either side.

name: Cloud Shadow
parking_note: Park at a roadside pullout on the left of Flagstaff Road, about 1.2 miles above the bridge at Capstan Rock.

name: Combat Rock
parking_note: From Loveland drive about 17 miles up US 34 through Big Thompson Canyon, turn right onto Devil's Gulch Road, then right again onto the dirt Storm Mountain Road. Use the pullout on the north side; there is plenty of room.

name: Dude's Throne
parking_note: Pass through the Aspen Meadow Campground and continue to the lot at Dude's Fishing Hole; the crag is visible from the parking area.

name: Duncan's Ridge
parking_note: Park in the lot on the east side of Centennial Dr, about 1/2 mile north of CR-38E (1 mile south of CR-42C). It is shared with the Piano Keys boulders; hike west up the hogback about 5 minutes to the ridge.

name: Englemann Canyon (submitted as Ruxton Canyon, Manitou Springs)
Five Point to a Fist Crag
Gill Boulder, The
parking_note: Use the picnic area lot at the canyon's final bridge; the boulder stands a few steps from the parked cars.

name: Graduation Boulder and Post-Graduation B
parking_note: Drive about 0.7 miles up the canyon road from the park entrance and pull off beside the boulder.

name: High Wire Crag
parking_note: Use the roadside pullouts along US 6 just short of the bridge near Tunnel 2; the north side is the easier choice.

name: Left Side
parking_note: A rough dirt road runs most of the way to the cliff rim; a high-clearance vehicle can park right at the top, while a low car has to stop short and walk a long way in.

name: Lion's Den, The
parking_note: From Lyons, drive up US 36 for about four miles, turn left near the cottages, take the road to the left of their driveway, and follow it roughly a mile and a half to a parking lot.

name: Lower Grotto Wall
parking_note: Roughly nine miles up the Independence Pass road from Aspen, a wide pullout sits on the left just after a switchback, and the wall rises directly above it.

name: Ruckman Cave
parking_note: A pullout about 1.3 miles up the canyon holds roughly eight cars and sits directly opposite the Meat Wall.

name: North Face
parking_note: Pull off at one of the roadside spots on Highway 14 just beyond the tunnel west of Mishawaka, then cross over to the foot of the rocks.

name: Ouray Rotary Park-Rink Wall
parking_note: Drive about a mile north from central Ouray on US 550 toward Ridgway, turn in at the hockey rink on the right, and park near the public restrooms. The cliff is a few steps away.

name: Phases Rock (submitted as Beginner Toprope Area near Tabernash & Hurd Creek)
Piano Ridge
parking_note: Use the lot on the east side of Centennial Drive, roughly half a mile north of County Road 38E.

name: Smelter Gulch
parking_note: Park at the Smelter Mountain trailhead in the first dirt lot, then contour into the gulch; the cliffs are about eight minutes away.

name: Sweet Willie (submitted as Teal Campground Roadside Boulder)
White Cliff
parking_note: Take Frisco exit 201 and drive west on I-70 for a bit under a mile, then pull off beside the aspens near the forest service sign.

name: Willow Creek Pass Fins -- 99 Mile Rock
Boot Hill
parking_note: Use the southernmost parking area at the Prison Camp Campground off the lower Catalina Highway.

name: Southern Wall
parking_note: Park in the old highway department lot off Highway 260 east of Payson; the approach trail begins at the southwest corner of the lot.

name: Diamond Buttress
parking_note: Use the small pullout just east of the larger rocky-mound lot on the south side of US-60; the large lot serves the Pond.

name: Egg, The
parking_note: Drive to the turnaround on N 20th St and park on the Egg boulder side of the road, opposite the private property.

name: Green Slabs (SW Face)
parking_note: Pull off at mile marker 9.9 of the Catalina Highway, on the uphill (eastbound) shoulder, just short of where the road passes through a cut in the ridge. The crag is the formation touching the road.

name: Library, The
parking_note: Pull off on the east side of the highway just south of the East Verde bridge, about two miles north of Payson; the walk to the cliff starts from there.

name: Upper Wall
parking_note: Drive east from Payson on Highway 260 to about milepost 270.8 and take the paved pull-off on the right. Leave the car on the pavement edge without blocking the road.

name: Overlook, The
parking_note: The Overlook is on the east side of Highway 89A at the top of Oak Creek Canyon, just before the switchbacks. Use the paved lot, but if staying past 4:30 pm park across the highway because the gates are locked then.

name: Sweet Rock Routes
parking_note: Park about 2.0 mi along Forest Road 687 from the Middlemarch Rd junction at the Sweet Rock / Isle of Ewe pullout area; free primitive camping. The road is rough dirt.

name: Bad Rock Canyon
parking_note: Pull into the wide gravel turnout beside the highway; the problems start just above it.

name: The Friends Of The Bitter Groot
Main Area
parking_note: Leave the car at the Palisade Campground parking area outside Red Lodge; the trail to the formation starts there.

name: Sparerib Area
parking_note: Drive south on Highway 191 and leave the car in the big dirt area beside the river just beyond the 35 mph bridge.

name: Tier 1 Left Side Boulder(s)
parking_note: Use the Boulder Loop Trail lot just south of the Albany Covered Bridge, off the Kancamagus Highway about six miles west of Conway. If the bridge is shut, leave the car on the highway side and walk across.

name: Tier 3 Boulders
parking_note: Park near the Albany Covered Bridge off the Kancamagus Highway, where Passaconaway Road meets it. A lot at the Boulder Loop Trail start sits a short distance south of the bridge.

name: Tier 1 Right Side of Trail Boulder
Campground Boulders
parking_note: Use the Boulder Loop Trail lot just south of the Albany Covered Bridge on the Kancamagus Highway.

name: Main Face
parking_note: Leave the car in the small dirt lot on the right of Route 123 about a mile north of Marlow village; it holds around ten cars, with extra roadside space farther along.
